topic: Law Problem Questions: The IRAC Masterclass

copy.instagram:
We’ve all been there—staring at a 5-page law problem question, panicking because you don’t know where to start. Most students fall into the trap of writing a story about what happened to the parties. That’s how you end up with a 2:2. Examiners aren't looking for a narrative; they’re looking for a surgical application of the law.

Swipe to see how to pivot from 'storytelling' to 'scoring'.

[Slide 1: The 2:2 Trap] Writing long essays that retell the facts without isolating the cause of action or legal defenses.
[Slide 2: The 1st Class Blueprint] Systematic IRAC execution: Isolate the dispute, cite the specific statute/precedent, apply the law to the facts, and state your conclusion.

copy.facebook:
Law students, let’s talk about the dreaded problem question. I see so many of you getting bogged down in the facts, retelling the story of the case rather than dissecting the legal issues. It’s a common trap that keeps good students stuck at a 2:2.

To move up to a First, you need to master the IRAC method:

• Issue: Clearly identify the legal point at play.
• Rule: Cite the specific statute or leading precedent.
• Application: This is the meat of your answer—apply the law to the specific facts provided.
• Conclusion: Give a decisive, evidence-based verdict.
